## 2026-09-29 — Mobile nav: avatar-only identity chip (top bar + drawer)
Context: card asks that on mobile/small screens the nav identity chip (photo + username + #id)
collapse to just the photo, both in the top bar and in the sliding mobile menu. Weighed
trivial/haiku vs standard/sonnet. The chip markup already carries `hide-sm` on its meta text;
two deliberate CSS overrides in `src/styles/Navigation.css` (`.nav3-mobile-right .nav3-user-meta`
and `.drawer-head-right .nav3-user-meta`, `display:flex !important`) force it back on. The fix is
flipping those rules to hide the meta — CSS only, no logic branches, no motion change (the drawer's
slide-in is untouched, so the motion→opus override does not apply).
Decision: trivial / haiku (low). Sonnet was defensible for the responsive-breakpoint judgment
(meta hides at ≤640px via `hide-sm`, while the mobile layout starts at ≤900px), but the spec says
"mobile and small screens", so hiding it wherever the mobile chip renders is the obvious default.
Bias small; the failure policy escalates if haiku misses it.
Consequences: similar "hide/show an element per breakpoint in existing CSS" cards classify trivial/haiku.
